# Composed response cancellation after early helper reuse

First reconstruct the eleven early clean resets using the pinned earlier-reset package, including fresh compensation and cleanup. Its exact all-column target response determines which remapped kernel relations remain valid. Retain a pivot p with entrance E and donors D only if response(p) equals the XOR of donor responses, E lies inside each participant's first frame, pivots and donors are disjoint, and each shared donor serves a single entrance. Omit entries invalidated by physical aliases, changed responses, or changed first frames. Choose total entrance rank divisible by eight for exact bank packing.

Remove pivot columns from the initial zero-frame target compensation. Start each pivot at E, emit donor += pivot at E before the main word, and emit the inverse at the full frame after cleanup. The exact response relation cancels the omitted compensation. The entire composed program is replayed on all independent columns; the PR417/435 auditor additionally checks integer source-span legality. All unchanged rational frames and every nested/reflected transition are independently checked by the emitted-template audit.

Residual helper width is 8 minus its entrance rank. With eight replicas, width-seven slots are packed eight at a time with one width-eight slot; width-four slots pack sixteen at a time; remaining width-eight slots pack eight at a time. Every bank is full, every owner disjoint, every helper slot is accounted for, and all 72 emitted local invocations are checked. The emitted histogram, physical stock, coefficient growth, finite cost invoice, two exact moment engines, six bootstrap levels and 47 outer inequalities are recomputed after both transformations.

No separately reported numerical gains are added. The complex supplier is unchanged and all its phases are freshly replayed by the full wrapper. All-size compiler, dirty-bank, compressed-window, restored-work, tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces remain conditional assumptions. No new Lean theorem or unconditional multiplication bound is claimed.
